RAG is a method that lets AI models pull in up-to-date, relevant information from external sources (like documents or databases) before generating an answer. The trade-offs include needing good data pipelines, retrieval quality (chunking, embeddings), and guardrails to avoid injecting irrelevant or low-quality context. Key architecture patterns
- Classic RAG: Query → embed → vector search → top-k passages → prompt LLM → answer.
- Enhanced RAG: Add query rewriting (HyDE/multi-query), reranking (cross-encoder), and response verification (self-check or second-pass).
- Agentic RAG: Iterative retrieve-think-act loops (retrieve, draft, detect gaps, retrieve again).
- Modular RAG: Separate “lookup” (fast) vs “reasoning” (slow) prompts; cache frequent lookups.

Retrieval quality levers
- Chunking: 200–500 tokens with 20–50 token overlap for prose; page/section-level for manuals; code split by function/class.
- Indexes: HNSW (FAISS) for speed; DiskANN or Vespa for scale; hybrid (BM25 + vectors) improves recall on rare terms.
- Embeddings: Choose domain-tuned models if jargon-heavy; normalize to unit length; keep model/version consistent across corpus.
- Query boosts: Multi-query expansion, HyDE (LLM generates synthetic answer then embed), field-aware search (title > body > captions).
- Reranking: Cross-encoder rerank top 50 to top 5 for precision; big impact on hallucinations.

Prompting and context construction
- Structure: System: role + guardrails; Context: citations with titles/snippets; Task: constraints (cite sources, say “not found”).
- Budget: Fit 1–2k tokens of the most relevant, deduplicated content; avoid near-duplicates.
- Citations: Attach IDs/URLs to each passage and require the model to reference them inline.

Hallucination and safety controls
- Answerability check: If retrieval confidence low (e.g., mean cosine < threshold, or reranker score low), ask for clarification or say “insufficient info.”
- Grounded generation: “Only use provided sources; if absent, say so.” Penalize unsupported claims in evals.
- Guard PII/Secrets: Classify and redact before indexing; apply row/field-level ACLs at query time.

Freshness and maintenance
- Ingestion: Incremental sync with change detection (hashes/ETags); keep an “effective date” field for recency boosting.
- Observability: Track query → retrieved docs → answer → user feedback; surface top zero-result or low-confidence queries for content fixes.

Evaluation (automated and human)
- Datasets: Curate 100–500 real queries with gold answers and cited passages.
- Metrics:
  - Retrieval: nDCG@k, Recall@k.
  - Generation: Faithfulness (LLM judge), answer correctness (LLM or task-specific), citation coverage.
  - UX: Time-to-first-token, full latency, deflection rate, user rating.
- Regression tests: Lock in prompts and thresholds; rerun on every model/index update.

Latency and cost
- Fast path: Smaller reranker or skip rerank for easy queries (high lexical match); cache frequent results.
- Parallelism: Run vector and keyword search in parallel; prefetch for follow-ups.
- Batching: Batch embeddings and reranking calls; use streaming responses for perceived speed.

Minimal starter stack (Python)
- Storage/index: FAISS or Chroma for quick starts; Weaviate/PGVector/Elastic+ES-knn for production.
- Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large or local (bge-m3) if data stays on-prem.
- Rerankers: Cohere rerank or open-source cross-encoders (ms-marco variants).
- Orchestration: LangChain/LlamaIndex for prototypes; consider a light custom layer for production.
- Eval: Ragas or custom harness with LLM-as-judge plus human spot checks.

Implementation checklist
- Define scope: What questions must be answerable? What’s out of scope?
- Data prep: Source list, access controls, cleaning, chunking strategy, metadata schema.
- Retrieval baseline: Hybrid search, k=20, rerank to 5; set similarity thresholds.
- Prompt: System + strict citation rules + refusal policy; few-shot examples with good citations.
- Guardrails: Answerability gate, max answer length, banned topics if needed.
- Observability: Log all steps with IDs; add feedback thumbs-up/down with optional comments.
- Iterate: Fix top failure modes weekly (content gaps, chunking tweaks, prompt adjustments).

Key architecture patterns
- Classic RAG: Query → embed → vector search → top-k passages → prompt LLM → answer.
- Enhanced RAG: Add query rewriting (HyDE/multi-query), reranking (cross-encoder), and response verification (self-check or second-pass).
- Agentic RAG: Iterative retrieve-think-act loops (retrieve, draft, detect gaps, retrieve again).
- Modular RAG: Separate “lookup” (fast) vs “reasoning” (slow) prompts; cache frequent lookups.

Retrieval quality levers
- Chunking: 200–500 tokens with 20–50 token overlap for prose; page/section-level for manuals; code split by function/class.
- Indexes: HNSW (FAISS) for speed; DiskANN or Vespa for scale; hybrid (BM25 + vectors) improves recall on rare terms.
- Embeddings: Choose domain-tuned models if jargon-heavy; normalize to unit length; keep model/version consistent across corpus.
- Query boosts: Multi-query expansion, HyDE (LLM generates synthetic answer then embed), field-aware search (title > body > captions).
- Reranking: Cross-encoder rerank top 50 to top 5 for precision; big impact on hallucinations.

Prompting and context construction
- Structure: System: role + guardrails; Context: citations with titles/snippets; Task: constraints (cite sources, say “not found”).
- Budget: Fit 1–2k tokens of the most relevant, deduplicated content; avoid near-duplicates.
- Citations: Attach IDs/URLs to each passage and require the model to reference them inline.

Hallucination and safety controls
- Answerability check: If retrieval confidence low (e.g., mean cosine < threshold, or reranker score low), ask for clarification or say “insufficient info.”
- Grounded generation: “Only use provided sources; if absent, say so.” Penalize unsupported claims in evals.
- Guard PII/Secrets: Classify and redact before indexing; apply row/field-level ACLs at query time.

Freshness and maintenance
- Ingestion: Incremental sync with change detection (hashes/ETags); keep an “effective date” field for recency boosting.
- Observability: Track query → retrieved docs → answer → user feedback; surface top zero-result or low-confidence queries for content fixes.

Evaluation (automated and human)
- Datasets: Curate 100–500 real queries with gold answers and cited passages.
- Metrics:
  - Retrieval: nDCG@k, Recall@k.
  - Generation: Faithfulness (LLM judge), answer correctness (LLM or task-specific), citation coverage.
  - UX: Time-to-first-token, full latency, deflection rate, user rating.
- Regression tests: Lock in prompts and thresholds; rerun on every model/index update.

Latency and cost
- Fast path: Smaller reranker or skip rerank for easy queries (high lexical match); cache frequent results.
- Parallelism: Run vector and keyword search in parallel; prefetch for follow-ups.
- Batching: Batch embeddings and reranking calls; use streaming responses for perceived speed.

Let’s kick off with a 5‑minute primer: AI agents (beginner).

The gist
- AI agents are software that can plan and act toward a goal with some autonomy, often using large language models (LLMs) plus tools (APIs, browsers, code).
- Think “smart assistant that can decide next steps,” not just “chatbot that answers.”

How they work (simple flow)
1) Goal/intake: You give a task or objective.
2) Planning: The agent breaks it into steps.
3) Tool use: It calls tools (search, code, database, email) to do steps.
4) Reflection: It checks results and decides what to do next.
5) Output: Delivers the result; may keep running on triggers or schedules.

Common types
- Task agents: One-off jobs (summarize a report, draft an email, scrape a site).
- Research agents: Search, read, extract, and synthesize sources.
- Data/code agents: Write/run code, clean data, build small scripts.
- Workflow/RPA agents: Automate repetitive business processes.
- Multi-agent systems: Several specialized agents collaborate (researcher, coder, reviewer).

Typical uses
- Personal: Trip planning, inbox triage, calendar scheduling, meal plans.
- Work: Lead list enrichment, report drafting, meeting notes, QA checks, basic analytics.
- Dev/data: Generate scripts, unit tests, ETL steps, SQL queries, dashboard stubs.

Benefits
- Saves time on repetitive and “glue” work.
- Can chain tools to complete end-to-end tasks.
- Good at first drafts and structured data extraction.

Limits and pitfalls
- Hallucinations: Confidently wrong outputs, especially without verification.
- Tool misuse: Poor parameter choices or wrong data source.
- Context limits: Misses details outside its input window.
- Compliance/security: Must avoid unsafe actions or leaking sensitive data.
- Costs/latency: Tool calls and long chains can get slow/expensive.

How to get started (practical)
- Pick one high-friction task you do weekly (e.g., summarize 5 links into a brief).
- Give a clear objective, constraints, and success criteria.
- Provide tools safely: read-only first (search/docs), then controlled write (drafts, staging).
- Add guardrails: max steps, cost/time caps, human approval gates.
- Log everything: inputs, tool calls, outputs; review early runs.

Lightweight tooling options
- No-code: Zapier/Make + AI steps; Notion or Airtable with AI; browser agents.
- Dev-friendly: LangChain, LlamaIndex, Microsoft AutoGen, OpenAI Assistants API.
- Browsing and code: Provide a search API, a read-only browser, a sandboxed code runner.

Evaluation tips
- Define “done”: exact fields, formats, and acceptance tests.
- Compare agent vs. simple prompt: only keep the agent if chaining adds value.
- Track precision/recall for extraction tasks; time saved for workflow tasks.

Safety checklist
- Scope tools narrowly; prefer least privilege.
- Strip or mask secrets; use vaults for API keys.
- Add allowlists for domains and actions.
- Human-in-the-loop for sends, purchases, or irreversible changes.

Jargon cheat sheet
- Tool calling: Model invokes functions/APIs you expose.
- Memory: Storing facts across steps/sessions (vector stores or databases).
- Reflection: Model critiques/repairs its own plan/output.
- Multi-agent: Several models/roles coordinate on a task.

What’s next
- Pick a pilot use case and I’ll help you design the prompt, tools, and guardrails.
